title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Salt Lake City, UT: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Salt Lake City: refinery, mining, aerospace and bridge work, Part C code choice and where Utah candidates test. Get a quote.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep for Salt Lake City and the Wasatch Front: A Six-Day Course
html:
Salt Lake City candidates preparing for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector examination can use the Atlantis NDT six-day CWI exam-prep course in two ways: study it online on their own schedule, or have their employer bring the six days to its shop or plant for a group. The American Welding Society runs the CWI examination and issues the certificate; Atlantis prepares people for it and certifies nobody. This page explains where welding inspectors work along the Wasatch Front, which code book makes sense for that work, how a Utah candidate gets to each part of the exam, and how the course fits around refinery shifts, mine maintenance and fabrication schedules. If you already know what you need, ask for a Salt Lake City CWI prep quote. The full course outline is on the national AWS CWI exam prep page.

Why welding inspection is steady work along the Wasatch Front

Few metro areas of this size put refining, copper smelting, military aircraft maintenance and rocket-motor manufacturing within an hour's drive of each other. Each of those industries welds, each has its own code culture, and each needs people who can read a procedure, check a welder's qualification and accept or reject a finished joint. That mix is why the CWI credential carries weight here even though Utah is not a shipbuilding or Gulf Coast refining state.

The refinery corridor north of downtown

The U.S. Energy Information Administration counts five petroleum refineries in the Salt Lake City area, clustered in North Salt Lake and Woods Cross, and notes that much of their crude arrives by pipeline from Utah, Colorado, Wyoming and Canada. Marathon Petroleum operates its Salt Lake City refinery there, and HF Sinclair runs its Woods Cross refinery a few miles north. Refinery repair and turnaround welding is done to procedures qualified under ASME Section IX, with process piping accepted to ASME B31.3 and pressure vessel repairs handled under the owner's in-service inspection program. A contractor sending pipe welders into a unit needs someone who checks fit-up, preheat, filler metal and welder continuity records before the first root pass, and that person is very often a CWI.

Copper mining and smelting on the west side of the valley

Rio Tinto's Kennecott Utah Copper operates the Bingham Canyon mine southwest of the city, with its smelter and refinery near Magna. Mining is hard on steel. Haul truck frames, shovel booms, crusher housings, chutes and conveyor structures crack and wear, and the repair welding that keeps them running is heavy, multi-pass work on thick sections, often with preheat requirements that crews are tempted to skip. Shops that rebuild that equipment, and the contractors who repair smelter structures, use inspectors who can judge weld size and profile, spot cracking at toes and recognize when a repair procedure has drifted from what was qualified.

Aerospace and defense to the north

Hill Air Force Base, between Salt Lake City and Ogden, is one of the large Air Force maintenance depots, and Northrop Grumman's Promontory operations in northern Utah build large solid rocket motors. Around them sits a supply chain of machine shops and fabricators that weld tooling, ground support equipment, test fixtures and structural assemblies. Some of that work is controlled by aerospace welding specifications rather than structural codes, which is why AWS D17.1 appears as a Part C option and why a few Utah candidates choose it.

Construction, bridges and pipelines

Steel-framed buildings, transit and airport projects, warehouse and data-center construction, and highway bridges keep structural fabricators and erectors busy across Salt Lake, Davis, Weber and Utah counties. Structural steel is usually built to AWS D1.1, and bridge steel for the state transportation department follows AWS D1.5. The crude and product pipelines feeding the refineries add pipeline construction and tie-in work, which is inspected to API 1104. Many building departments also require special inspection of structural welding under the building code, and CWIs are commonly the people who sign those reports.

Who asks for a CWI in Utah, and what they want from one

The credential means slightly different things to different employers. The table below is a practical guide to what Wasatch Front employers tend to expect, not a rule set; your employer's contract and specifications decide.

Employer typeWhat the CWI is expected to doCode most often in play
Structural fabricators and steel erectorsVerify fit-up, preheat and welder qualifications; visually accept fillet and groove welds; keep inspection records for the engineer of recordAWS D1.1
Bridge steel fabricatorsInspect to the stricter bridge provisions, including fracture-critical members where specifiedAWS D1.5
Refinery maintenance and turnaround contractorsReview WPS and PQR coverage, track welder continuity, inspect pipe welds before NDTASME Section IX with B31.3 or B31.1
Pipeline contractorsInspect girth welds, check procedure and welder qualification to the pipeline standardAPI 1104
Mining equipment rebuild shopsControl repair procedures on thick sections, check preheat and interpass temperature, judge crack-prone jointsAWS D1.1 or the customer's repair specification
Aerospace and defense suppliersInspect to the customer's aerospace welding specification and drawing notesAWS D17.1 or customer specifications
Special inspection agenciesPerform and document code-required welding inspection on building projectsAWS D1.1 under the building code

Boilers and pressure vessels add one more layer. In Utah, the Labor Commission's Boiler and Elevator Safety program administers the state boiler and pressure vessel rules, which are published in the Utah Administrative Code. A CWI does not replace the jurisdictional inspector, but repair work on covered equipment is welded and documented to codes a CWI is trained to read.

Picking a Part C code book when your work crosses industries

Part C is an open-book test on one code that you choose, and the choice matters more in Salt Lake City than in a single-industry town because many local inspectors move between refinery, structural and mining work. The options AWS listed on its CWI page in November 2026 included AWS D1.1 (2020 edition), API 1104 (22nd edition), AWS D1.2 for aluminum, AWS D1.5 (2020 edition), AWS D15.1 for railroad cars and locomotives, AWS D17.1 (2024 edition), an ASME choice that bundles Section IX with the B31.1 power piping and B31.3 process piping codes, and an ISO option.

  • Refinery and process plant people usually do best with the ASME option, because Section IX and B31.3 are the documents they already handle on turnarounds. See our notes on ASME Section IX and ASME B31.3.
  • Structural and mining shop inspectors usually choose AWS D1.1, which also governs most building special inspection.
  • Bridge fabrication staff should consider AWS D1.5, since its bridge-specific rules are what their audits check.
  • Pipeline crews working the lines that feed the refinery corridor should consider API 1104.
  • Aerospace supplier staff near Hill Air Force Base or the rocket-motor plants can weigh D17.1 against D1.1, depending on whether their shop's work is flight hardware or ground equipment.

A useful test: pick the book you would open at work next Monday. Familiarity with its layout saves minutes on every Part C question, and the code you certify on is the one employers will associate with your name. Study the edition AWS names for the exam, which can trail the newest edition in print.

Getting to each part of the exam from Salt Lake City

The CWI examination has three parts, and they are not taken in the same kind of place. AWS states that Parts A (Fundamentals) and C (Code Application) are computer-based tests delivered at Prometric centers, of which it lists more than 450 worldwide and over 100 in the United States. Use Prometric's site locator to find the center nearest you on the Wasatch Front once AWS has sent your confirmation letter with the eligibility code that Prometric needs for booking.

Part B, the practical, is different. AWS holds it at its own seminar and examination locations, typically on the weekend after an AWS seminar week at the same venue. When we checked the CWI training locations listed on aws.org in November 2026, no Utah city appeared, and the nearest listed city was Denver, Colorado. Locations change, so check the AWS Seminar and Exam Schedule before you plan, but most Salt Lake City candidates should budget for travel to sit the practical. Bring a valid driver's license or passport and a copy of your AWS confirmation letter. AWS sets application deadlines for the practical well ahead of the exam date, so apply early rather than waiting until your studying feels finished.

The AWS Utah Section and the local welding community

AWS organizes its members into local sections grouped in districts. Its section directory lists a Utah Section in District 20, alongside the Colorado, Southern Colorado, Idaho/Montana, New Mexico and Wyoming sections. Section meetings, plant tours and student events are where Salt Lake City welders meet working CWIs, fabrication managers and instructors. For a candidate that matters in a practical way: the experience you claim on your AWS application has to be verifiable, and the people who can vouch for your welding work are often the ones you meet through the section and through employers who are active in it. Check aws.org for the section's current contacts and meeting calendar.

Learning to weld locally, then counting the years

Many Utah CWI candidates started as welders, and the local technical college route still feeds the trade. Salt Lake Technical College, part of Salt Lake Community College, runs a welding program at its Westpointe Campus at 1060 North Flyer Way in Salt Lake City. Its published course list covers oxyacetylene welding, shielded metal arc, gas metal arc, flux cored arc and gas tungsten arc welding, plus oxy-fuel, plasma and air carbon arc cutting and gouging, welding math and blueprint reading, with day and evening blocks.

That background helps in two ways. Completed trade or vocational courses count in the AWS eligibility table: AWS lists four years of welding-related experience for candidates with that training, against five years with a high school diploma alone. And the processes, positions and joint preparations a welder learns in the booth are exactly what Part A asks about. What the booth does not teach is inspection vocabulary, symbol reading at speed, metallurgy beyond the basics and code navigation, which is where most welders turned inspectors need the preparation.

How the six days fit a Salt Lake City schedule

Atlantis has no classroom or office in Utah; its offices are in Houston and Hyderabad. The course reaches Salt Lake City candidates in one of two forms.

Individuals studying online

You receive a study plan laid out over the six course days, course materials, original practice questions written to the published AWS topic areas, timed practice papers and a route for sending questions to an instructor. There are no set class times. That suits refinery operators and maintenance welders on rotating shifts, and it suits turnaround hands who disappear into a unit for weeks and need to pause. A common pattern is to work through the fundamentals and code material in the months before a planned outage ends, then do the timed papers in the last stretch before the exam.

Employers bringing the course on site

A fabricator in West Valley City, a mining equipment rebuild shop near Magna or a contractor yard in Davis County can book the six days as one block taught inside its own building to several employees together. On-site delivery lets the practical exercises use your own fillet gauges, bridge cam gauges and weld samples, and lets the code day work in the book your shop actually builds to. Even when the boss books the week, each welder files a personal AWS application, carries the eyesight and experience requirements alone and settles AWS charges separately.

What the six days cover

The structure is identical online and on site. Day 1 builds welding vocabulary: processes, joint design and welding symbols to AWS A2.4, with terms to AWS A3.0. Day 2 covers metallurgy, mechanical and destructive testing, discontinuities and what causes them, nondestructive testing methods, safety and inspector ethics. Day 3 is practical preparation for Part B: measuring weld size and profile, applying procedure and qualification records, and accepting or rejecting against supplied criteria. Day 4 works inside your chosen code book. Day 5 is timed practice for all three parts with review of every miss. Day 6 targets weak areas and ends with an exam-day and application checklist. The AWS CWI training page describes each day in detail.

Exam rules worth knowing before you commit

  • Governing standard. In November 2026 AWS listed QC1:2016-AMD1, Specification for AWS Certification of Welding Inspectors, as the governing document.
  • Format. Fundamentals, the first part, is a 150-question paper. The practical mixes 46 questions with hands-on tasks done on gauges and replica specimens AWS hands you at the venue. Code Application lets the book sit open on the desk and runs somewhere between 50 and 65 questions. A score below 72 percent on any one part means that part is not passed.
  • Eligibility. Experience requirements fall as education rises, from twelve years with less than eighth-grade schooling to one year with a welding engineering or welding technology bachelor's degree. The table is on the national page and on aws.org.
  • Vision. AWS asks for a near-vision test at Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, corrected or uncorrected, plus color perception, recorded on its form by a qualified examiner.
  • Keeping the certificate. Once issued, the credential runs on a nine-year cycle under AWS rules, with a renewal application expected at the three-year and six-year marks.
  • Fees. Examination and seminar charges belong to AWS, which posts the current figures on aws.org. Our budget worksheet for the CWI exam helps a Utah candidate add the Part B trip to the plan.

For a broader view of what the credential demands and returns, read CWI requirements and career impact, and for how candidates fare on each part, CWI results by exam part.

CWI alongside NDT on the Wasatch Front

A CWI judges welds mostly by eye and by document review. When a refinery, rocket-motor supplier or bridge fabricator needs to see inside a weld or find a surface crack too fine for the eye, it calls for nondestructive testing, and that work is done by technicians certified by their employer under ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Plenty of Utah inspectors hold both kinds of qualification. Atlantis delivers SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for the region, described on the NDT training in Salt Lake City page; welding inspectors most often add VT Level 2 or magnetic particle and ultrasonic methods. You can rehearse visual inspection steps in the Practical NDT welding workshop simulator. For local inspection services, see visual testing in Salt Lake City.

Refinery inspectors often ask about API 510, 570 and 653 as the next step. API runs those certifications under its own rules, and Atlantis does not train for them; the API inspector guide explains how they work, and CWI vs API 577 vs ASNT Level II sets the three side by side.

Neighboring CWI pages, and how to start a Salt Lake City quote

Inspectors who work across the Mountain West and the Pacific Northwest may find these pages useful too: CWI exam prep in Denver, CWI exam prep in Phoenix and CWI exam prep in Portland.

To scope the course, tell us whether it is for one person or a group, each candidate's education and welding-related experience in outline, the Part C code book each person intends to choose, and, for on-site delivery, where the facility is and which weeks avoid your outages or production peaks. Put that in the Salt Lake City enquiry form; a reply comes back from us within one business day.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis CWI classroom in Salt Lake City?
faq.a: No. Atlantis has offices in Houston and Hyderabad. Salt Lake City candidates study the six-day course online with instructor support, or their employer has the six days delivered at its own facility for a group. See the course outline.

faq.q: Where do Salt Lake City candidates take the CWI exam?
faq.a: Parts A and C are computer-based tests at Prometric centers, so most candidates can test locally after AWS sends the eligibility code. Part B, the practical, is held at AWS seminar and examination locations; in November 2026 the aws.org location list showed no Utah city, with Denver the nearest. Check the AWS schedule for current dates.

faq.q: Which code book should a Utah refinery inspector choose for Part C?
faq.a: Most refinery and process plant inspectors choose the ASME option, which pairs Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, because those are the documents used on turnarounds. Structural and mining shop inspectors usually choose AWS D1.1, and pipeline inspectors API 1104.

faq.q: Does AWS have a local section in Salt Lake City?
faq.a: Yes. The AWS section directory lists a Utah Section in District 20. Check aws.org for its current contacts and meetings.

faq.q: Does Atlantis certify me as a CWI after the six days?
faq.a: No. AWS runs the examination and grants the CWI credential. A Utah candidate still files a personal AWS application, satisfies the experience and eyesight requirements, and has to clear Fundamentals, Practical and Code Application.

faq.q: Do welding courses at a Utah technical college count toward CWI eligibility?
faq.a: Completed trade or vocational courses appear in the AWS eligibility table: AWS lists four years of welding-related experience with that training, compared with five years with a high school diploma. AWS decides what qualifies, so confirm on aws.org.

faq.q: Can a mining equipment shop near Magna run the course for its welders?
faq.a: Yes. Employers can have the six days delivered at their facility, using their own gauges, weld samples and code. Request a quote with headcount and preferred weeks.

faq.q: Are the practice questions copied from the AWS exam?
faq.a: No. Atlantis writes its own questions against the subject list AWS makes public and never sees the real paper.

faq.q: Should a Salt Lake City welding inspector also get NDT certification?
faq.a: Often, yes. Refineries, aerospace suppliers and bridge fabricators need NDT performed by technicians certified by their employer under ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Atlantis offers that training; see NDT training in Salt Lake City.

faq.q: Does Atlantis train for API 510, 570 or 653?
faq.a: No. Atlantis offers API inspector exam prep as separate self-paced online courses. The API inspector guide explains how they work.
